plain_english: largest increase in transverse width between two consecutive resampled analysis points
worked_example: sequence [+10, +3, -2, +1] -> the biggest rise is +10, so max_positive_delta_W = 10

plain_english: most negative transition, i.e. the largest single contraction
worked_example: sequence [+10, +3, -2, +1] -> the most negative entry is -2, so min_delta_W = -2

plain_english: median of only the transitions where the width grew
worked_example: positives are [+10, +3, +1]; their median is 3, so median_positive_delta_W = 3

plain_english: share of transitions in which the width increased
worked_example: 3 of the 4 transitions are positive, so fraction_positive_delta_W = 0.75

plain_english: sum of every increase, i.e. total growth ignoring the shrinking steps
largest increase divided by the time gap it happened in (um per ms)
worked_example: if the +10 um rise took 0.0068 ms then max_positive_width_rate = 10 / 0.0068 = 1471 um/ms

plain_english: median of the positive rises after each is divided by its own time gap
worked_example: the positive rises [+10, +3, +1] become rates, and we take the middle one

plain_english: share of transitions with a positive rate -- identical to fraction_positive_delta_W because every time gap is positive, so dividing by it cannot flip a sign
worked_example: 3 of 4 positive -> 0.75, exactly the same number as fraction_positive_delta_W
